questions.prompt: Which function has zeros at 0, 4, and −1/2?
questions.hint: Set each factor equal to 0. Which choice gives 0, 4, and −1/2?
questions.solution: x = 0 gives 0. x − 4 = 0 gives 4. 2x + 1 = 0 gives −1/2. So f(x) = x(x − 4)(2x + 1).

teach.title: Multiplicity and the degree
text: The exponent on a factor is the multiplicity of its zero. Odd multiplicity: the graph crosses. Even multiplicity: it touches and turns around.
The multiplicities add up to the degree.

steps: 2 has multiplicity 3 (odd): the graph crosses there, flattening out as it goes through.
−1 has multiplicity 2 (even): the graph touches the x-axis and turns around.

teach.title: Write a polynomial from zeros with multiplicity
text: Write each factor as many times as its multiplicity, then multiply.

example.problem: Write a polynomial in standard form with a zero at 1 of multiplicity 2 and a zero at −3 of multiplicity 1.

questions.prompt: f(x) = (x + 3)²(x − 6)⁵. What is the multiplicity of the zero 6?
questions.hint: Look at the exponent on the factor (x − 6).
questions.solution: (x − 6) appears 5 times, so the zero 6 has multiplicity 5.

questions.prompt: f(x) = (x + 3)²(x − 6)⁵. What does the graph do at x = −3?
choices: It touches the x-axis and turns around.
It does not reach the x-axis there.
It crosses the x-axis and flattens out.
questions.hint: Find the multiplicity of the zero −3. Is it even or odd?
questions.solution: (x + 3)² gives the zero −3 with multiplicity 2. Even multiplicity means the graph touches the x-axis and turns around.

questions.prompt: f(x) = x³(x − 2)(x + 4)². What is the degree of f?
questions.hint: Add up the multiplicities. (x − 2) has an exponent of 1.
questions.solution: 3 + 1 + 2 = 6. The degree is 6.

questions.prompt: Factor f(x) = x³ + 8x² + 16x. What are the zeros and their multiplicities?
questions.hint: Take out x first. Then the trinomial is a perfect square.
questions.solution: x(x² + 8x + 16) = x(x + 4)². The zero 0 has multiplicity 1 and the zero −4 has multiplicity 2.

questions.prompt: f(x) = 3x⁴ − 12x³ + 12x². Where does the graph touch the x-axis without crossing?
choices: Nowhere. It crosses at every zero.
questions.hint: Factor out 3x². Which zeros have an even multiplicity?
questions.solution: 3x²(x² − 4x + 4) = 3x²(x − 2)². Both zeros, 0 and 2, have multiplicity 2, so the graph touches at both.

questions.prompt: f(x) = (2x − 1)³(x + 4). Which describes the zero that comes from (2x − 1)³?
questions.hint: Solve 2x − 1 = 0. The exponent is the multiplicity.
questions.solution: 2x − 1 = 0 gives x = 1/2. The exponent 3 is the multiplicity. 3 is odd, so the graph crosses.

questions.prompt: The graph of a cubic touches the x-axis at x = 2 and crosses it at x = −1. Which function could it be?
questions.hint: Touching means even multiplicity. Crossing means odd multiplicity. A cubic has degree 3 in all.
questions.solution: The zero 2 needs multiplicity 2: (x − 2)². The zero −1 needs multiplicity 1: (x + 1). Degree 2 + 1 = 3. f(x) = (x − 2)²(x + 1).

questions.prompt: A polynomial has a zero at 3 with multiplicity 2 and a zero at −1 with multiplicity 2. Which function in standard form could it be?
questions.hint: The factors are (x − 3)² and (x + 1)². Multiply (x − 3)(x + 1) first, then square it.

questions.prompt: f(x) = −x²(x − 5)(x + 1)³. List the zeros where the graph crosses the x-axis, separated by commas.
questions.hint: The graph crosses at zeros with odd multiplicity.
questions.solution: 0 has multiplicity 2 (even), so the graph touches there. 5 has multiplicity 1 and −1 has multiplicity 3, both odd, so the graph crosses at 5 and −1.

teach.title: Solve by factoring
text: Step 1: move all terms to one side so the equation equals 0.
Step 2: factor the polynomial completely.
Step 3: set each factor equal to 0 and solve for x.

teach.title: When a factor won't factor
text: If a quadratic factor will not factor, solve it with square roots or the quadratic formula.
Simplify every radical. If x² equals a negative number, the solutions are imaginary: x² = −4 gives x = ±2i.

steps: 5x = 0 gives x = 0. x² − 4 = 0 gives x = ±2. x² + 4 = 0 gives x² = −4, so x = ±2i.

questions.prompt: Solve 12x³ − 3x² = 0. Type every solution, separated by commas.
questions.hint: Take out the GCF 3x².
questions.solution: 3x²(4x − 1) = 0. 3x² = 0 gives x = 0. 4x − 1 = 0 gives x = 1/4. Solutions: 0, 1/4.

questions.prompt: Solve 2x³ − 16x² − 40x = 0. Type every solution, separated by commas.
questions.hint: Take out the GCF 2x, then factor the trinomial.

questions.prompt: Solve x³ = x² + 20x. Type every solution, separated by commas.
questions.hint: Move everything to one side first: x³ − x² − 20x = 0.

questions.prompt: Solve x³ − 8x² + 16x = 0. Type every different solution, separated by commas.
questions.hint: x² − 8x + 16 is a perfect square trinomial.
questions.solution: x(x² − 8x + 16) = x(x − 4)² = 0. Solutions: 0 and 4 (4 has multiplicity 2, but you list it once).

questions.prompt: Solve 2x³ − 3x² − 32x + 48 = 0. Type every solution, separated by commas.
questions.hint: Four terms: try grouping.

questions.prompt: Solve 4x³ + 5x² − 16x − 20 = 0. Type every solution, separated by commas.
questions.hint: Group the first two terms and the last two terms.

questions.prompt: What is the first step to solve x³ + 3x² = 24x + 72?
choices: Move every term to one side so the equation equals 0.
Take the cube root of both sides.
Factor x³ + 3x² and set it equal to 24x + 72.
questions.hint: Factoring only works when one side is 0.
questions.solution: Move everything to one side first: x³ + 3x² − 24x − 72 = 0. Dividing by x would lose solutions.

questions.hint: Move everything to one side, then group: x²(x + 3) − 24(x + 3).

teach.title: Imaginary solutions from cubes
text: A sum or difference of cubes leaves a quadratic factor that does not factor.
Use the quadratic formula on it: x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac)) / 2a. A negative under the root gives imaginary solutions.

teach.title: Word problems
text: Set the model equal to the given value. Move everything to one side, factor, and solve.
Keep only answers that make sense: no negative lengths, times, or years.

example.problem: A box has sides (x − 3), (x − 1), and (x − 8), and a volume of 33x. Find the sides.
steps: Group: x²(x − 12) + 2(x − 12) = (x² + 2)(x − 12) = 0. The only real solution is x = 12.

questions.solution: x² − 8 = 0 gives x = ±√8 = ±2√2. x² + 8 = 0 gives x² = −8, so x = ±2i√2.

questions.hint: 512 = 8³. Factor as a sum of cubes, then use the quadratic formula.
Treat x² as one variable: two numbers that multiply to −42 and add to 1.
questions.solution: (x² + 7)(x² − 6) = 0. x² = 6 gives ±√6. x² = −7 gives ±i√7.

questions.hint: Factor like a trinomial in x²: (4x² − 1)(x² + 9).
questions.solution: 4x² − 1 = 0 gives x² = 1/4, so x = ±1/2. x² + 9 = 0 gives x² = −9, so x = ±3i.

questions.hint: Move everything to one side: 5x³ − 3x² + 30x − 18 = 0. Then group.

questions.prompt: A business's revenue in thousands of dollars is R(t) = 2t³ − 12t² + 3t + 57, where t is years since 1995. In what year did revenue reach $75,000?
questions.hint: Set R(t) = 75 (it is in thousands). Then group.

questions.prompt: A species' population is p(t) = −t⁴ + 56t² + 240, where t is years. About how many years until the species is extinct? Round to the nearest hundredth.
questions.hint: Extinct means p(t) = 0. Treat t² as one variable.
questions.solution: −t⁴ + 56t² + 240 = 0 gives t⁴ − 56t² − 240 = 0, so (t² − 60)(t² + 4) = 0. t² = 60 gives t = √60 ≈ 7.75 years. (Negative time and t² = −4 do not make sense.)

questions.prompt: A trapezoid has bases x + 5 and 5x − 1, height x² + 1, and area 30x + 20 square feet. Find the area in square feet.
questions.hint: Set ½(base₁ + base₂)(height) = 30x + 20, solve for x, then find the area.
questions.solution: ½(6x + 4)(x² + 1) = (3x + 2)(x² + 1) = 3x³ + 2x² + 3x + 2. Set equal to 30x + 20: 3x³ + 2x² − 27x − 18 = 0, so (x² − 9)(3x + 2) = 0 and x = 3. Area = 30(3) + 20 = 110 square feet.

teach.title: Do not divide by x
text: Dividing both sides by x throws away the solution x = 0.
Instead, move every term to one side and factor out the x.

steps: Dividing by x first would give only ±2 and miss 0.

teach.title: Equations in quadratic form
text: If the exponents are 4 and 2, treat x² as one variable and factor like a trinomial.
Then solve each x² = k. If k is positive, x = ±√k.

steps: Two numbers that multiply to 9 and add to −10: −1 and −9. So (x² − 1)(x² − 9) = 0.
x² = 1 gives x = ±1. x² = 9 gives x = ±3.

questions.prompt: Solve x(x − 6)(2x + 3) = 0. Type every solution, separated by commas.
questions.hint: The equation is already factored. Set each factor equal to 0.
questions.solution: x = 0. x − 6 = 0 gives x = 6. 2x + 3 = 0 gives x = −3/2. Solutions: 0, 6, −3/2.

questions.prompt: Solve 5x³ − 20x² = 0. Type every different solution, separated by commas.
questions.hint: Take out the GCF 5x².
questions.solution: 5x²(x − 4) = 0. 5x² = 0 gives x = 0. x − 4 = 0 gives x = 4. Solutions: 0, 4.

questions.prompt: Solve x³ + 2x² − 15x = 0. Type every solution, separated by commas.
questions.hint: Take out x, then factor the trinomial.

questions.prompt: Solve x³ = 9x. Type every solution, separated by commas.
questions.hint: Do not divide by x. Move 9x to the left side first.
questions.solution: x³ − 9x = 0, so x(x² − 9) = x(x + 3)(x − 3) = 0. Solutions: 0, 3, −3.

questions.prompt: Solve x⁴ − 17x² + 16 = 0. Type every solution, separated by commas.
questions.hint: Treat x² as one variable: two numbers that multiply to 16 and add to −17.
questions.solution: (x² − 1)(x² − 16) = 0. x² = 1 gives ±1. x² = 16 gives ±4. Solutions: 1, −1, 4, −4.

questions.prompt: Solve x³ − 5x² − 4x + 20 = 0. Type every solution, separated by commas.
questions.hint: Four terms: group them.

questions.prompt: Solve 2x³ + 3x² = 8x + 12. Type every solution, separated by commas.
questions.hint: Move everything to the left side, then group.

questions.prompt: Solve x³ + 4x² + 4x = 0. Type every different solution, separated by commas.
questions.hint: Take out x. The trinomial left over is a perfect square.
questions.solution: x(x² + 4x + 4) = x(x + 2)² = 0. Solutions: 0 and −2 (−2 has multiplicity 2, but you list it once).

questions.hint: Group: x²(x − 3) − 2(x − 3).
questions.solution: (x² − 2)(x − 3) = 0. x − 3 = 0 gives x = 3. x² = 2 gives x = ±√2.

teach.title: When x² is negative
text: If a factor gives x² = −k with k positive, the solutions are imaginary: x = ±i√k.
Simplify the radical: √−36 = 6i and √−8 = 2i√2.

teach.title: Word problems with grouping
text: Set the model equal to the value you are given. Move everything to one side and factor by grouping.
Keep only answers that make sense, like a positive number of years.

example.problem: A company's profit, in thousands of dollars, is P(t) = t³ − 4t² + 2t + 10, where t is years after 2015. In what year was the profit $18,000?
steps: t = 4. t² = −2 has no real solution.

questions.hint: Take out x. Then x² + 49 = 0 means x² = −49.

questions.solution: x² − 9 = 0 gives x = ±3. x² + 9 = 0 gives x² = −9, so x = ±3i.

questions.hint: Treat x² as one variable: two numbers that multiply to −10 and add to −3.
questions.solution: (x² − 5)(x² + 2) = 0. x² = 5 gives ±√5. x² = −2 gives ±i√2.

questions.hint: Difference of cubes: (x − 3)(x² + 3x + 9). Use the quadratic formula on the second factor.
Sum of cubes: (2x + 1)(4x² − 2x + 1). Use the quadratic formula on the second factor.
Group: x²(x − 2) + 9(x − 2).
Move everything to one side: x⁴ − 4x² − 45 = 0. Then treat x² as one variable.
questions.solution: (x² − 9)(x² + 5) = 0. x² = 9 gives ±3. x² = −5 gives ±i√5.

questions.prompt: A company's profit, in thousands of dollars, is P(t) = t³ − 5t² + 3t + 20, where t is years after 2018. In what year was the profit $35,000?
questions.hint: Set P(t) = 35 (it is in thousands). Move everything to one side, then group.

questions.prompt: A box has length x − 1, width x − 2, and height x − 3, in inches. Its volume is 10x cubic inches. What is the volume in cubic inches?
questions.hint: Set (x − 1)(x − 2)(x − 3) = 10x. Expand, move 10x over, then group.
questions.solution: (x − 1)(x − 2)(x − 3) = x³ − 6x² + 11x − 6. Set equal to 10x: x³ − 6x² + x − 6 = 0. Group: x²(x − 6) + 1(x − 6) = (x² + 1)(x − 6) = 0, so x = 6. Volume = 10 · 6 = 60 cubic inches (sides 5, 4, and 3).

questions.hint: Square everything in the parentheses first.
questions.solution: (−6a⁴b³)² = 36a⁸b⁶. Times −2ab⁵: 36 · −2 = −72, a⁸·a = a⁹, b⁶·b⁵ = b¹¹. Answer: −72a⁹b¹¹.

questions.hint: Simplify the top first, then divide.
questions.solution: Top: 40x²y². Divide by 10x⁶y²: 4x²⁻⁶y⁰ = 4x⁻⁴ = 4/x⁴.

questions.prompt: Write −2x² + x⁴ + 3 in standard form and classify it.
questions.hint: Highest exponent first. Then name the degree and count the terms.
questions.solution: Standard form: x⁴ − 2x² + 3. Degree 4 is quartic, and 3 terms is a trinomial.

questions.prompt: Write −7 + 5m³ + 9m − 3m² in standard form and classify it.
questions.hint: Order the exponents 3, 2, 1, 0. Count all the terms.
questions.solution: Standard form: 5m³ − 3m² + 9m − 7. Degree 3 is cubic, and 4 terms is a polynomial.

questions.hint: Change every sign in the second part. −(−8h⁴) is +8h⁴.

questions.prompt: Without graphing: which function has this end behavior? As x → −∞, f(x) → ∞; as x → ∞, f(x) → −∞.
questions.hint: Up on the left and down on the right means odd degree and a negative leading coefficient.
questions.solution: −x³ − 12x + 20 has degree 3 (odd) and leading coefficient −1 (negative).

questions.prompt: Look at the graph. Is the degree even or odd, and is the leading coefficient positive or negative?
questions.hint: Compare the two ends, then look at the right end.
questions.solution: The left end goes up and the right end goes down. Opposite ways means odd. The right end goes down, so the leading coefficient is negative.
